findings.title: Signed integer overflow when converting decoded OSQ samples to unsigned 8-bit PCM
findings.message: In the OSQ audio decoder's sample-format conversion loop for AV_SAMPLE_FMT_U8P, the decoded 32-bit sample `src[n]` is added to 0x80 before being clamped with av_clip_uint8(). Because `src[n]` is a plain `int32_t` and `0x80` is interpreted as a regular `int` literal, the addition `src[n] + 0x80` is performed using signed 32-bit int arithmetic. When the decoded residual/prediction value in `src[n]` is close to INT32_MAX (e.g. 2147483565), adding 0x80 (128) overflows the range of a 32-bit signed int, which is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by UBSan/oss-fuzz ("signed integer overflow: 2147483565 + 128 cannot be represented in type 'int'"). The intent of the code was to bias the sample into unsigned range before clamping to [0,255], but the arithmetic is done before the clamp is able to bound the value, so extreme (attacker/fuzzer supplied, malformed-bitstream-derived) values of src[n] trigger UB rather than being safely clipped.
findings.suggestion: Perform the addition in a wider integer type (e.g. int64_t / long long) before clamping, so that the intermediate sum cannot overflow the type used for the arithmetic, and only the final clamped value is narrowed to uint8_t.

ground_truth.root_cause: The bias addition needed prior to clamping (`src[n] + 0x80`) was implemented using ordinary 32-bit int arithmetic without first widening the operands, so extreme decoded sample values (which are only bounds-checked after the addition, inside av_clip_uint8) can overflow signed 32-bit int range before the clamp has a chance to bound them.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Signed integer overflow when converting decoded OSQ samples to unsigned 8-bit PCM
